# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the Kripke benchmark on a single AWS ARM-based CPU node in Kubernetes.
# It leverages the Flux Operator to manage the distributed workload.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A unique name for the MiniCluster instance to prevent collisions.
  name: kripke-minicluster-1
  # The Kubernetes namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of MPI tasks (ranks) to run. This can be more than the number of nodes (pods).
  tasks: 4
  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict checking of the manifest.
    strict: true
  # Do not delete the pods after the job is complete, to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # Flux-specific configuration.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture for the Flux instance container, required for ARM instances.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Use an ARM-compatible image for the Flux view.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
  # Pod-level specifications for the MiniCluster pods.
  pod:
    resources:
      # Resource limits for the pod.
      limits:
        # Request an AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) device for high-performance networking.
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
      # Resource requests for the pod.
      requests:
        # Request an AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) device.
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to be executed by Flux. The `flux run` prefix is added automatically.
      # This runs the kripke benchmark with default settings.
      command: kripke
      # This container is not the main job launcher; Flux handles that role.
      launcher: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest runs the Kripke benchmark on a single AWS ARM-based CPU node.
# It addresses the previous structural error by placing the resource requests and limits
# under the container specification (`spec.containers[0].resources`) as required by the CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A unique name for the MiniCluster instance to avoid collisions with previous attempts.
  name: kripke-minicluster-2
  # The Kubernetes namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of MPI tasks (ranks) to run. This can be more than the number of nodes (pods).
  tasks: 4
  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict checking of the manifest.
    strict: true
  # Do not delete the pods after the job is complete, to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # Flux-specific configuration.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture for the Flux instance container, required for ARM instances.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Use an ARM-compatible image for the Flux view.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux. There should only be one container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to be executed by Flux. The `flux run` prefix is added automatically.
      command: kripke
      # This container is not the main job launcher; Flux handles that role.
      launcher: false
      # Resource requests and limits are applied directly to the container.
      resources:
        limits:
          # Request an AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) device for high-performance networking.
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          # Request an AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) device.
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

manager.name: Scaling Study for Kripke

context.environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes to run across nodes
context.scale:
Strong scale kripke to minimize FOM.
You MUST choose a kripke configuration at the smallest size (1) that you use for subsequent sizes.
Stop when you determine the application is no longer weak scaling.
context.optimize:
Minimize the kripke figure of merit for Grind time. 
You MUST choose a problem size running 'kripke' with (-n) at size (1) that you MUST use at all larger sizes. You can change other kripke parameters as you change size.
You MUST NOT change the primary problem size after the first scaling size (1).
You MUST make an effort to increase problem size at the first scaling size (1) until the job times out.
You MUST decrease problem size if the pod is OOMKilled and try to optimize around that point.
You MUST increase the problem size ONLY at the first scaling size until it stops improving in performance.
You MUST set flux.optionFlags to "-o cpu-affinity=per-task"
At large sizes, you MUST adhere to the same resource limits, requests, and node selectors.
You MUST set environment variables for MPI to use EFA with libfabric.
You MUST adhere to ONE node (64 tasks) for the initial optimization.
context.resources: Your nodes include the 64 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3).
context.details:
You MUST run on only one node. 
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9. Otherwise, do not change or set it.
If you are using an ARM instance you MUST also set flux.arch: "arm".
